### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it), /:object/import/jobs (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via preserveAudit (literal, a string literal in NonEntryExecutionContextField))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via preserveAudit (literal, a string literal in NonEntryExecutionContextField))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via preserveAudit (literal, a string literal in NonEntryExecutionContextField))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via preserveAudit (literal, a string literal in NonEntryExecutionContextField), /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it), /:object/import/jobs (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via preserveAudit (literal, a string literal in NonEntryExecutionContextField))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via runImport (symbol, a top-level function), /:object/import (route, bridged from symbol runImport — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `32b4e882c0aaba55140a61447ce6b624f2d467aa` — the merge of head `2917976c67aaab21295f6d5173208c9970f213bc` into base `fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 32b4e882c0aaba55140a61447ce6b624f2d467aa && git checkout 32b4e882c0aaba55140a61447ce6b624f2d467aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c 2917976c67aaab21295f6d5173208c9970f213bc && git checkout -B drift-repro fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c && git merge --no-ff 2917976c67aaab21295f6d5173208c9970f213bc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fbcbcf124f2aa49259b837bc74cdbf4d08b46b3c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2917976c67aaab21295f6d5173208c9970f213bc`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-08T12:10Z by an isolated at-tier subagent of the seat session. Inputs: card #22183 (body and every comment), PR #22282 (body, 17-file list, net diff `main`...head over merge base `9f0de32a`, +732 / -34), and the 33 check-runs on the head. The dispatch order, the `Claim:` and the `ACCEPT` comment were not inputs to the judgment; the dev's `os-dev-report` was read as claims to verify. Git reads only (`fetch` into review refs, `diff`, `show`, `grep`); nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set (the import door):

1. **right** — With `ImportRequest.createMissingOptions: true`, the import's insert, update and dry-run `validate` admit, per field, exactly the `select` / `radio` value or multi-value item that coercion kept: `coerceFieldValue` reports what it kept (never what it matched), `coerceRow` aggregates it per field, `runImport.writeCtxFor` puts it on the write context, and the validator's two option arms test `keptOptions.includes(String(value))` only after the `allowed` miss. The admitted set is bounded to values that came through this import's own coercion; every other value outside `options` is still refused (the `Other` / `Stray` controls in the validator pins; the `w1` / `w2` plain-write controls end to end).
2. **right** — A batched create carries the union of its rows' kept values (`ctxForRows` on `insertManyData` and `createManyData`): one call, one context. Its consequence — a `beforeInsert` hook that moves a kept value onto a sibling row of the same batch is admitted — is bounded to that import's kept values and is stated in the PR's acceptance notes. A per-row context on a batched write would be a protocol change outside this card.
3. **right** — A row that kept nothing, and every write with the option off, carries the import's `writeCtx` unchanged (`not.toHaveProperty('keptOptionValues')` pins; the option-off control), so a normal import's writes are byte-identical to before.
4. **right** — A field bound to a shared picklist that did not resolve stays refused whatever the write names: `picklistUnresolved()` returns before the kept check in both arms.
5. **right** — Readonly values are unchanged: `shapeOnly` returns before either arm's option constraint, and the engine's two `'only'` passes are untouched.
6. **right** — Non-import writes are unchanged. A stored kept value sent back on a later write is judged against `options` and refused; a write that leaves the field out is not judged on it; picking an option is accepted. That is the frozen-not-bricked reading the triage asked for, and the option arm reads the payload only, never the stored row.
7. **right** — The field's option list is never written; no metadata write exists anywhere in the diff.
8. **right** — Type coverage is aligned on both sides through the spec: coercion keeps for `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` (`select`, `radio`) and `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` (`multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`), and the validator dispatches on `select` / `radio` non-multiple versus `isMultiValueField`, both from `@objectstack/spec`. The describe names `select / radio / multiselect`; enforcement also reaches `checkboxes` and an options-bearing `tags`. The claim is narrower than the enforcement, which is the permitted direction; recorded, not a defect.

Public surface:

9. **right** — `ExecutionContext.keptOptionValues` (optional; per field name, an array of strings) is a declared, typed, server-only signal beside `skipStateMachine` and `preserveAudit`; no `??` tolerance in any consumer. It is not client-reachable: `assembleExecutionContext` builds the envelope from resolved identity only (`entryFields` spreads nothing from a request), the field is classified non-entry so the closed set compiles, no transport parses a `*DataRequest` body wholesale (none found under rest, metadata-protocol, plugins, services, runtime, adapters), REST binds `context` from `resolveExecCtx` on create, update and both import routes, and `action-execution.ts` builds its own. The key also rides on every engine options shape that embeds `ExecutionContext` (find, count, aggregate, delete, per the regenerated `data-engine.mdx`), inert there exactly as its siblings are.
10. **right** — `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json` gains `kernel/ExecutionContext:keptOptionValues`; `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` passed in `Type Check · source gates`.
11. **right** — The `ImportRequest.createMissingOptions` describe states only what is enforced (kept as written, admitted on this import's writes with the dry run included, options unchanged, a later write judged again, an unresolved picklist still refused); the runtime string carries no tracker number.
12. **right** — `@objectstack/core`: `coerceFieldValue`'s result gains an optional `keptOptionValues`; `coerceRow`'s result gains `keptOptionValues` (always present, empty when nothing was kept) — additive for readers; `RunImportOptions` and `ImportProtocolLike` are unchanged.
13. **right** — `@objectstack/objectql`: `ValidateRecordOptions.keptOptionValues` is optional; `validateOne` gains a defaulted internal parameter read by the two option arms only; the four engine call sites (validate preview, batched insert, both update paths) pass `context?.keptOptionValues`. The refusal still names the declared options, so no message key moves.
14. **right** — The three `content/docs/references` pages are regenerated, not hand-written; no release-owned page is touched.
15. **right** — No governed path, no REST route or query-parameter change, no ADR decision reversed: the free-form `multiselect` exemption (ADR-0078, `allowed.length === 0`) is untouched, and `invalid_option` keeps its catalog meaning.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22183-import-kept-option-values.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — **right**. The diff widens the accept set on the import door and adds optional public keys on three released packages; `yes` takes at least `minor`. Nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. No other released package changes (rest and metadata-protocol pass the context through untouched). `skip-changeset` would be wrong and is not used.
- PR body `Clause-②: yes (the enforce route widens ...)` reads as `yes` with no arm under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (the parenthetical opens with reasoning, not an arm-family word), consistent with the changeset's `yes (widening)`; the claim's declaration is the same spelling.
- `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared; none found.
- Deviation 1 (surface breach: `execution-context.zod.ts`, `assemble-execution-context.ts` and its test, `engine.ts`, generated artifacts) — **answered, accepted on the diff's own merits**: the signal needs a declared home and `ExecutionContext` is where its import siblings live; the compile-time closed field set forces the classification; the validator is reachable only through those engine call sites; the artifacts are generated. All inside the claim's declared packages.
- Deviation 2 (shared clone deepened, `origin/main` advanced) — **answered**: process, disclosed; every diff cited is anchored on the merge base `9f0de32a`; no effect on the head.
- Deviation 3 (whole-repo build for `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) — **answered**: process; no effect on the head.
- Deviation 4 (objectql / spec suites and typechecks cited at `4305775d`) — **answered, verified by a git read**: `git diff --stat 4305775d2 2917976c` is five files — the changeset, the three generated reference pages, one line of `assemble-execution-context.test.ts`; `packages/objectql` and `packages/spec/src` are byte-identical between the two heads. CI's `Test Core` on the final head is the run of record (named below).
- Deviation 5 (attribution per AGENTS.md rather than the harness reminder) — **right**; AGENTS.md wins.
- Out-of-scope 1 (objectui `refusedOptionValue` preview still marks a kept value on a writable field; its docblock sentence becomes false) — **correctly outside this repo's card; escalated to the seat** as the objectui follow-up to file once this lands. Not a blocker.
- Out-of-scope 2 (import undo cannot restore an off-list prior value; now also reachable after a kept import followed by an update-mode import) — **acceptance note is the right carrier**: pre-existing posture for option-removed values, not reproduced, and the undo write in `rest-server.ts` is outside the card. Not a blocker.
- Out-of-scope 3 (objectui empty-diff save resends the whole record and is refused on a row holding a kept value) — **acceptance note is right**: existing posture for any stored off-list value; the dispatch's stop condition keeps the option-arm widening to the import door.
- Reviewer's own flags: the batch-union admission (①.2) and the `checkboxes` / `tags` reach beyond the describe's wording (①.8) are recorded above; neither changes the verdict.

### Check-runs on the head, read at the same act

33 check-runs: 24 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 7 `in_progress`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`. A run in progress is not a pass: this record's verdict is on ①–③ above, and the landing still waits on those seven concluding `success`. Concluded `success` include `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)`, `(2/3)`, `(3/3)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Check PR Size`.
